summary: The bill amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to modify eligibility criteria for certain loans by striking two clauses in Section 502(3)(C) that restrict use for plant acquisition, construction, conversion, or expansion.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Small Business Investment Act to relax eligibility criteria for certain SBA 504 loans by striking two clauses in Section 502(3)(C). This change would likely make more small businesses eligible for government-backed loans for real estate and equipment, indirectly expanding the scope of a federal lending program and its associated contingent liabilities or spending. The effect is minor and not a direct appropriation, but it moves in the direction of expanded government activity in lending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection. It solely modifies loan eligibility rules under an existing SBA program.
No provisions address healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms. The legislation is limited to small business fixed-asset financing.
The bill has no connection to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No references to immigration policy, border enforcement, visas, or related protections appear in the text.
The legislation does not address reproductive rights, abortion access, or funding restrictions.
No provisions involve military spending, defense procurement, or national security funding.
